Title: OEE

args.text: When the description says that the process waits until one of several alternative external events occurs, model the alternatives as intermediate catch events following an event-based gateway, rather than as a decision task or exclusive-gateway choice.

trace.reason: Check documented guidance relevant to modeling the stated restart/disconnection triggers and determine whether a proposed guideline would duplicate or conflict with it.

result.rule: Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Give the outgoing sequence flows of an event-based gateway no conditionExpression; the first occurring target event selects the path.
Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.

args.text: When a process description says that the flow continues upon one of several alternative external events, model the alternatives as catching events selected by an event-based gateway, rather than as a decision about which outcome to choose.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers the event-based modeling supported by the description.

result.rule: When the description says that one of several alternatives is selected, or that an activity may occur: Model the choice or optional activity with an appropriate gateway, and reconnect the resulting paths before subsequent common work.
When the description says that a decision or outcome is communicated to a person: Model the communication as a distinct activity; do not treat the decision gateway itself as the communication.

When the description says that an action may be required based on a stated condition and also describes a later process outcome.: Model and label the decision gateway according to whether that action is required; do not use the later outcome as the gateway’s decision.

When the description states a final activity but does not explicitly identify the outcome that ends the process: Use a generic end-event label rather than inferring a specific business outcome from that activity.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use dataObjectReference for process-instance data and dataStoreReference for persistent information available beyond one process instance.
Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.

args.text: When the description says that a process collects or obtains information from a source, model the act of retrieving that information as an explicit activity before using it.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing learned guideline already addresses explicit information retrieval activities.

result.rule: When the description says information must be gathered or choices made before the main work begins: Model the gathering or choice as a distinct activity and connect it before the main work; do not use the main-work workflow as a substitute for it.

When the description explicitly states that an actor performs an action that initiates the described process: Model the stated action as an activity in the actor’s scope; do not use a start event representing the resulting occurrence as a substitute for that activity. Represent the process start separately with an appropriate start event.

When the description explicitly states that a matter is brought to completion after a decision or another activity: Model the stated completion work as an activity on the applicable path before the process outcome.

When the description states that a distinct body of work is started and also describes the work performed within it: Model the stated act of starting the work as a separate activity before the workflow that performs it; do not use that workflow, a subprocess, or a start event as a substitute for the activity.
